citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》 (天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692)
citations.field: PDF p. 87; printed p. 75; headword 口 and entry prose, verified against attached scan pixels
citations.text: The scanned entry identifies 口 as a pictograph shaped like a human mouth and gives ‘mouth’ as its basic meaning. It cites an oracle-bone use, 詩·豳風·鴟鴞 using 口 in the mouth sense, and bronze use as a clan sign. It also proposes that ancient forms were generally written in two strokes, with three-stroke forms possibly appearing by Han times; this stroke-history claim is the book's account, not independently confirmed here. I visually checked the headword, forms, prose and entry ending on the attached PDF p. 87 scan. PDF p. 88 begins with a continuation for 噲, not 口.
